text.p: Britain's Railtrack Plc said on Thursday that it would be spending 5.7 billion pounds ($9.2 billion) on day-to-day maintenance over a period of 10 years.
In its 1996/97 network management statement the British rail infrastructure firm said it would spend 8.3 billion pounds on renewal investment over the same period.
The company said it would also spend 1.9 billion pounds during the same period.
Railtrack chairman Robert Horton said its new spending plans marked a "new dynamic phase in the regeneration of the nation's railway system".
"Ten years from now Britain will have a railway that is second to none -- both in the quality of its infrastructure and in the dependability of its train service," he added.

Railtrack has drawn up a programme of 26 major renewal and enhancement projects, each costing 25 million pounds. Thirty enhancement schemes to bring in more freight on the rail network are also being considered.
